sentences.text: Porphyrio claytongreenei is an extinct species of swamphen, a type of rail belonging to the family Rallidae.
Its specific name, claytongreenei, honors Warren Clayton-Greene, the landowner where the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was found.
Worthy and colleagues formally described this bird in 2026.
The name pays tribute to Clayton-Greene for protecting fossil sites on his property by fencing them off from livestock.
This extinct rail lived in Zealandia during the Calabrian stage of the Pleistocene epoch.
The genus Porphyrio existed from the Zanclean to the Holocene, between 5.333 and 0 million years ago.
